beats: Hook: cut one matrix by columns and the next by rows, and a whole conversation between GPUs disappears.
Where the weight is: Q, K, V and output projections and the MLP up and down projections are all matrix multiplies (GEMMs).
Two cuts: by columns each GPU makes a slice of the output (AllGather to join); by rows each makes a partial sum (AllReduce to add).
The trick: column then row: each GPU's slice feeds straight into its own row piece; one AllReduce per block, two per layer.
Attention fits too: the column cut is a cut by heads.
Leftovers: LayerNorm and dropout run on full activations on every GPU; sequence parallelism splits them by token.
Same price: AllReduce = AllGather + ReduceScatter, so TP + SP moves the same data.
Critical path: the next layer waits for the talk; it can only be hidden block by block (fine-grained).
Numbers: over a 25 GB/s network the talk takes 4x the compute; over NVLink the compute is ~3x the talk: keep TP inside a node.
Cover (line_cover_l06_03; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): four bakers each hold one vertical strip of a grid-paper sheet; together the strips make the whole sheet.
